doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

title: Views on the state of the country
summary: She expresses alarm about politics, racism, the internet and global threats, and says it makes her focus on playing music; Rowe agrees.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yeah. Well here’s not a softball question to sort of wrap up to. I’m interested in what artists have to think about the state of our country. So you could pass on the question but if you want to offer something I’d be happy to hear about it.

Sure. I think we’re in a very dark and dangerous point in our history right now with the anti-democratic, not just direction but I feel like we might even have a civil war because it just seems like what’s been happening with the Republican party and the fact that they still embrace Trump after everything, it’s just like they — are you a Republican?

I hope not. They just — it’s like they don’t think and they’re so angry and their morals, they have no morals. They’ll do whatever it takes to get what they want. They’ll cheat, they’ll lie, they’ll steal. And it was really an eye-opener when Trump got elected because I had no idea that there were that many people that would vote for somebody like that. I mean I knew they existed but I had no idea of the number. And what’s happening with race I mean it’s hard to — I guess that’s a plus of the internet age and everybody having a camera on their phone, maybe we’re just finding out more about this stuff. I mean I knew that there were issues but I had no idea that there’s as much racism and hatred in this country. I mean I knew there was but not to the degree that it is. And then of course the whole thing with Russia — I mean Putin could set off a nuclear bomb at any time and then there’s China. I think that that all contributes to me just wanting to do what I want to do, play the music I want to play with the great musicians I get to play with and what do you think?

Yes it makes it all that much more valuable. And I’m — I’ve felt like I’ve been an optimist most of my life but it’s harder and harder to be one now. And I agree with everything you’ve said and it seems like technology has brought out the worst in many people, the best in some but the worst in a lot of people. And it’s okay to share all of it and try to convince others to be that way, because I can.

I can. And you can find a little group of people, like-minded people, no matter what you’re into you can find those people on the internet whereas before the internet you wouldn’t find all these hundreds or thousands of people that think like you so you would keep it down. I don’t know. I think we’re in trouble.
Yeah. Well let’s think happy thoughts, like a major third against a minor blues.
Only temporarily. Try it. Play like a little line and hit the minor third and then go up to the major third from it, and then go back down.
